title: How Clarence Thomas Came to Reject Affirmative Action

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，你每晚都要带上300件最珍贵的收藏去工作，然后把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Ketroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·凯特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Yesterday we heard from Americans reflecting on the end of affirmative action and decades of race-conscious admissions at colleges across the country.
sentences.zh: 昨天我们听到了美国人对平权法案终结以及全国高校数十年来种族意识招生政策的看法。

sentences.en: Now we turn to one of the most powerful figures behind that reversal,
sentences.zh: 现在，我们将目光转向推动这一逆转的最具影响力的人物之一，

sentences.en: Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas, the second Black justice to sit on the court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院大法官克拉伦斯·托马斯，他是第二位进入最高法院的黑人大法官。

sentences.en: Thomas spent years opposing affirmative action, a policy that arguably shaped his career.
sentences.zh: 托马斯多年来一直反对平权法案，而这一政策可以说塑造了他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Abby Van Sickle explains the impact of affirmative action on Justice Thomas' life and how he helped bring about its demise.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事艾比·范·西克尔将解释平权法案对托马斯大法官人生的影响，以及他是如何推动其终结的。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月14日，星期五。

sentences.en: Abby, a couple weeks ago, as we know, the Supreme Court ended affirmative action by a 6-3 majority.
sentences.zh: 艾比，我们知道几周前，最高法院以6比3的多数票终结了平权法案。

sentences.en: And one of the most interesting voices in all of this was Clarence Thomas, who wrote, in his opinion, this scathing takedown of this longstanding feature of American education.
sentences.zh: 而其中最引人注目的声音之一来自克拉伦斯·托马斯，他在意见书中对这一美国教育界的长期特征进行了严厉抨击。

sentences.en: And so, I want to understand, how did he arrive at this opinion?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想了解他是如何得出这一观点的？

sentences.en: So, I cover the Supreme Court for the New York Times, and I have spent the last several weeks just trying to understand and dig into the life of Clarence Thomas,
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》报道最高法院，过去几周我一直在努力了解和深挖克拉伦斯·托马斯的生平，

sentences.en: in part to really be able to understand and articulate his views on affirmative action.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是为了真正理解并阐述他对平权法案的看法。

sentences.en: And to understand Justice Thomas, I think you really have to start with where he grew up.
sentences.zh: 要理解托马斯大法官，我认为必须从他的成长环境说起。

sentences.en: He grew up in Pinpoint, Georgia, in just really extreme poverty.
sentences.zh: 他在佐治亚州的平点（Pinpoint）长大，生活在极度贫困之中。

sentences.en: And he moved with his sibling and his mom to Savannah.
sentences.zh: 后来他和兄弟姐妹以及母亲搬到了萨凡纳。

sentences.en: And in his autobiography, which he reads for the audiobook, he describes what that was like.
sentences.zh: 在他亲自朗读的有声版自传中，他描述了那段生活。

sentences.en: The only running water in our building was downstairs in the kitchen, where several layers of old linoleum were all that separated us from the ground.
sentences.zh: 我们楼里唯一的自来水在楼下的厨房里，那里只有几层旧油毡布把我们和地面隔开。

sentences.en: And his mom was working as a maid, and she couldn't take care of Clarence and his brother, so they went to live with his grandparents.
sentences.zh: 他母亲当时做女佣，无法照顾克拉伦斯和他的兄弟，所以他们去和祖父母住在一起。

sentences.en: And that's important to know because his grandfather becomes this really central figure in his life.
sentences.zh: 了解这一点很重要，因为他的祖父成了他生命中至关重要的人物。

sentences.en: Despite the hardships he had faced, there was no bitterness or self-pity in his heart.
sentences.zh: 尽管面临重重困难，但他心中没有苦涩，也没有自怜。

sentences.en: As for bad luck, he didn't believe in it.
sentences.zh: 至于坏运气，他根本不信。

sentences.en: Instead, he put his faith in his own unaided effort, the one factor in life that he could control.
sentences.zh: 相反，他把信念寄托在自己不懈的努力上，这是他生活中唯一能掌控的因素。

sentences.en: And he taught me to do the same.
sentences.zh: 他也教我这样做。

sentences.en: In addition to growing up in poverty,
sentences.zh: 除了在贫困中长大，

sentences.en: Clarence Thomas was also growing up in the segregated South.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯也是在种族隔离的南方长大的。

sentences.en: In the 50s and 60s, blacks steered clear of many parts of Savannah.
sentences.zh: 在50和60年代，黑人对萨凡纳的许多地方都避之不及。

sentences.en: No matter how curious you might be about the way white people lived, you didn't go where you didn't belong.
sentences.zh: 无论你对白人的生活方式有多好奇，不该去的地方你绝不会去。

sentences.en: When he was a teenager,
sentences.zh: 当他还是个少年时，

sentences.en: Thomas decided he wanted to be a priest, and he enrolled at a nearly all-white seminary.
sentences.zh: 托马斯决定成为一名神职人员，并进入了一所几乎全是白人的神学院。

sentences.en: And just as Thomas has written and talked about this and has explained how difficult it was, that he was really taunted and singled out because of his race.
sentences.zh: 正如托马斯所写和所谈到的那样，他解释了当时有多么艰难，因为他的种族，他确实受到了嘲弄和针对。

sentences.en: And maybe the most upsetting experience for him happened after he graduated high school and went to seminary in Missouri.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，最令人不安的经历可能发生在他高中毕业并前往密苏里州的神学院之后。

sentences.en: He's there in 1968 when Martin Luther King is assassinated.
sentences.zh: 1968年马丁·路德·金遇刺时，他就在那里。

sentences.en: I walked into the dormitory one April afternoon and heard someone shout that Martin Luther King Jr.
sentences.zh: 四月的一个下午，我走进宿舍，听到有人大喊马丁·路德·金博士

sentences.en: had been shot.
sentences.zh: 被枪杀了。

sentences.en: That's good, another student replied.
sentences.zh: “那太好了，”另一名学生回答道。

sentences.en: I hope the son of a bitch dies.
sentences.zh: “我希望那个狗娘养的死掉。”

sentences.en: And that's a really seminal moment for Justice Thomas.
sentences.zh: 这对托马斯大法官来说是一个非常关键的时刻。

sentences.en: His brutal words finished off my vocation and my youthful innocence about race.
sentences.zh: 他那残忍的话语终结了我的神职追求，也终结了我对种族问题的青春天真。

sentences.en: So it's at this point that Clarence Thomas decides to abandon his plans to become a priest and instead to get a liberal arts education.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，克拉伦斯·托马斯决定放弃成为神职人员的计划，转而接受文科教育。

sentences.en: And he has talked about how a nun encouraged him to look at Holy Cross College up in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 他曾谈到一位修女是如何鼓励他去看看马萨诸塞州的圣十字学院的。

sentences.en: And in the fall of 1968, he enters college there.
sentences.zh: 1968年秋天，他进入那所大学。

sentences.en: And that coincides with a time when colleges and universities across the country, in the wake of Martin Luther King's assassination,
sentences.zh: 那段时期恰逢全国各地的学院和大学在马丁·路德·金遇刺后，

sentences.en: are trying to recruit and support Black students.
sentences.zh: 都在努力招募和支持黑人学生。

sentences.en: This is the height of the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 那是民权运动的高峰期。

sentences.en: And Justice Thomas is in a small group of Black students at this liberal arts college.
sentences.zh: 托马斯大法官当时是这所文理学院中一小群黑人学生中的一员。

sentences.en: And he joins together with those students.
sentences.zh: 他与这些学生团结在一起。

sentences.en: They form a student union for Black students to really try to actually have a meaningful presence on the campus.
sentences.zh: 他们成立了一个黑人学生会，试图在校园里真正拥有有意义的影响力。

sentences.en: The more I read about the Black Power movement, the more I wanted to be a part of it.
sentences.zh: 我读的关于黑人权力运动的书越多，就越想成为其中的一员。

sentences.en: He talks about his admiration for Malcolm X, and he writes about going to demonstration and being part of this movement and how important that was in shaping his worldview.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了对马尔科姆·X的钦佩，并写道自己参加示威活动，成为这场运动的一部分，以及这对他塑造世界观有多么重要。

sentences.en: What was the point of working within the system?
sentences.zh: 在体制内工作有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: Segregation, lynchings, Black code, slavery, the endless litany of injustices raced through my head.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离、私刑、黑人法典、奴隶制，无数的不公正像连珠炮一样在我脑海中闪过。

sentences.en: Surely the time for politeness and nonviolent protest was over.
sentences.zh: 礼貌和非暴力抗议的时代显然已经结束了。

sentences.en: He very much considers himself to be a liberal and in some ways a Black nationalist at that point in his life.
sentences.zh: 在那段人生阶段，他非常自认为是自由派，在某种程度上也是黑人民族主义者。

sentences.en: Wait, I just, can we pause for a second?
sentences.zh: 等等，我能暂停一下吗？

sentences.en: You're telling me Clarence Thomas, one of the most iconic conservatives on the Supreme Court, maybe the most famous Black conservative ever, was a radical.
sentences.zh: 你是说克拉伦斯·托马斯，最高法院最具标志性的保守派之一，也许是有史以来最著名的黑人保守派，曾经是个激进分子？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To me, this came as a surprise when I started reading and really digging into this because of how we all know Justice Thomas now.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，当我开始阅读并深入研究这一点时，感到非常惊讶，因为我们现在都知道托马斯大法官是什么样的人。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he's starting to question his views.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他开始质疑自己的观点。

sentences.en: The beast of rage kept on gnawing at my soul, but the more I saw of radicalism, the more I doubted that it had any answers to offer me.
sentences.zh: 愤怒的野兽不断啃噬着我的灵魂，但我看到的激进主义越多，就越怀疑它是否能给我任何答案。

sentences.en: And he also goes to a demonstration in Harvard Square.
sentences.zh: 他还去参加了哈佛广场的一次示威活动。

sentences.en: He describes it as getting pretty violent and that that really leads him to feel like his views are jeopardizing how hard he has worked to get this education
sentences.zh: 他形容那次活动变得相当暴力，这让他真正感到自己的观点正在危及他为获得教育所付出的努力，

sentences.en: and to keep himself on track so that he's not headed back into poverty in Savannah.
sentences.zh: 以及让他保持正轨，以免重回萨凡纳的贫困生活。

sentences.en: He ends up graduating from Holy Cross and going to Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 他最终从圣十字学院毕业，进入了耶鲁法学院。

sentences.en: And he is so excited.
sentences.zh: 他当时非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He gets to campus and then pretty much right away, he starts to have doubts.
sentences.zh: 他来到校园，但几乎立刻就开始产生怀疑。

sentences.en: Affirmative action, though it wasn't yet called that, had become a fact of life at American colleges and universities.
sentences.zh: 平权法案，尽管当时还不叫这个名字，已经成为美国高校生活中的一个事实。

sentences.en: This is in the fall of 1971.
sentences.zh: 那是1971年的秋天。

sentences.en: And he comes in the same year that Yale Law School starts an affirmative action program.
sentences.zh: 他入学的同一年，耶鲁法学院启动了一项平权行动计划。

sentences.en: And before long, I realized that those Blacks who benefited from it were being judged by a double standard.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，我就意识到那些从中受益的黑人正受到双重标准的评判。

sentences.en: As much as it stung to be told that I'd done well in the seminary despite my race, it was far worse to feel that I was now at Yale because of it.
sentences.zh: 尽管被告知我尽管种族出身却表现出色让我感到刺痛，但更糟糕的是，我觉得自己现在在耶鲁是因为这个原因。

sentences.en: He talks about and writes about how the white students, he felt like they tokenized him, that he was viewed as somebody who only got into this elite school because he was Black.
sentences.zh: 他谈到并写道，白人学生让他感到自己被符号化了，他被视为一个仅仅因为是黑人才进入这所精英学校的人。

sentences.en: I felt as though I'd been tricked, that some of the people who claimed to be helping me were in fact hurting me.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己被骗了，那些声称在帮助我的人实际上是在伤害我。

sentences.en: It sounds like, Abby, even though Justice Thomas may have gotten into Yale in part because of these preferential policies that are just starting,
sentences.zh: 听起来，艾比，尽管托马斯大法官进入耶鲁可能部分是因为这些刚刚开始的优惠政策，

sentences.en: he's also bristling against the fact that these policies exist and that they may be in some way affecting how people perceive him on campus.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也对这些政策的存在感到愤怒，因为它们可能在某种程度上影响了人们在校园里对他的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: He does not like how he thinks he's perceived as less than as somebody who is only there because he's Black.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢人们认为他低人一等，认为他仅仅因为是黑人才出现在那里。

sentences.en: And he just reacts very strongly against this.
sentences.zh: 他对此反应非常强烈。

sentences.en: And he signs up for a curriculum of classes that he thinks are going to help improve himself.
sentences.zh: 他选修了一系列他认为能帮助提升自己的课程。

sentences.en: He's not taking civil rights law, he's taking corporate law, tax, bankruptcy, and really trying to, you know, define himself as somebody who's going to take those kind of classes
sentences.zh: 他没有选修民权法，而是选修了公司法、税法、破产法，并试图把自己定义为一个会选修这些课程的人，

sentences.en: and not be defined as a Black student.
sentences.zh: 而不是被定义为一个“黑人学生”。

sentences.en: And does he feel like that strategy works?
sentences.zh: 他觉得这个策略有效吗？

sentences.en: Like, does he feel as though he's able to dispel this notion that he's somehow less than because he's a Black student?
sentences.zh: 他是否觉得能够消除那种因为他是黑人学生就低人一等的观念？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It was futile for me to suppose that I could escape the stigmatizing effects of racial preference.
sentences.zh: 认为我能逃避种族优惠带来的污名化影响，这种想法是徒劳的。

sentences.en: And I began to fear that it would be used forever after to discount my achievements.
sentences.zh: 我开始担心，这种偏见会永远被用来贬低我的成就。

sentences.en: If anything, it seems to get worse in his time there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他那里的时间里，情况似乎变得更糟了。

sentences.en: He also writes about how he deeply regrets that he put anything about his race in his application because somehow he just can never shake the feeling that that just casts a shadow
sentences.zh: 他还写道，他非常后悔在申请中写下任何关于种族的内容，因为他总觉得那会给他的整个法学院经历蒙上一层阴影。

sentences.en: over his entire law school experience.
sentences.zh: 我对比我负责黑人遭受不公正待遇的白人偏执狂感到愤怒，但对比那些表面上不带偏见，

sentences.en: I was bitter toward the white bigots whom I held responsible for the unjust treatment of Blacks, but even more bitter toward those ostensibly unprejudiced whites
sentences.zh: 却假装站在黑人一边，实则利用他们来推进自己政治和社会目的的白人，我感到更加愤怒。

sentences.en: who pretended to side with Black people while using them to further their own political and social ends.
sentences.zh: 他在回忆录中写到了一个关于“自由派毒蛇”的类比。

sentences.en: He has this analogy that he writes about in his memoir about the liberal snake.
sentences.zh: 至少南方人对他们的偏执是直言不讳的。

sentences.en: At least Southerners were up front about their bigotry.
sentences.zh: 你知道他们从哪里来，就像佐治亚州的响尾蛇，总是让你知道它们什么时候准备攻击。

sentences.en: You knew exactly where they were coming from, just like the Georgia rattlesnakes that always let you know when they were ready to strike.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是说，在他长大的南方，人们对种族主义是公开的，没有隐藏。

sentences.en: And it's basically the idea that in the South, where he grew up, that people were open about their racism, that there was no hiding it.
sentences.zh: 那些虚伪的大城市白人则不同，只要你小心翼翼地同意他们，他们就给你提供帮助，但如果你开始表现得

sentences.en: Not so the paternalistic big-city whites who offered you a helping hand so long as you were careful to agree with them, but slapped you down if you started acting
sentences.zh: 好像不知道自己的位置，他们就会把你打倒。

sentences.en: as if you didn't know your place.
sentences.zh: 就像水腹蛇一样，他们毫无预兆地发起攻击，而现在我已经走进了攻击范围。

sentences.en: Like the water moccasin, they struck without warning, and now I had stepped within striking distance.
sentences.zh: 但在耶鲁，这种偏见被一种美好的外表所掩盖，他觉得这就像是在帮助他，但实际上他认为这依然在压制他。

sentences.en: But that at Yale, it's cloaked in this sort of nice veneer where it's like he's being helped, but actually he thinks it's still holding him down.
sentences.zh: 所以当他即将毕业时，他有一个年幼的儿子。

sentences.en: And so when he is about to graduate, he has a young son.
sentences.zh: 他结婚了。

sentences.en: He's married.
sentences.zh: 他背负着沉重的学生贷款，他是这样描述的。

sentences.en: He has crushing student loans, is how he describes it.
sentences.zh: 他面临着寻找一份高薪工作的巨大压力。

sentences.en: He is under a lot of pressure to find a great, well-paying job.
sentences.zh: 他写道，他所有的朋友都告诉他，你知道，你是耶鲁法学院的学生。

sentences.en: And he writes that all of his friends tell him, you know, you're at Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 你会有很多选择。

sentences.en: You are going to have your choice of places.
sentences.zh: 他面试了所有这些顶级律师事务所，但一个录取通知都没收到。

sentences.en: And he interviews with all of these top law firms, and he does not get a single offer.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是因为他被看不起，被这些律所合伙人视为一个仅仅因为是黑人才被录取的人。

sentences.en: And he credits that to being looked down on and viewed by these law firm partners as somebody who is only admitted because he's Black.
sentences.zh: 他认为这就是他找不到工作的原因。

sentences.en: And he thinks that's the reason he does not get a job.
sentences.zh: 现在我知道了，当耶鲁法学学位带有种族优惠的污点时，它值多少钱了。

sentences.en: Now I knew what a law degree from Yale was worth when it bore the taint of racial preference.
sentences.zh: 我感到羞辱和绝望。

sentences.en: I was humiliated and desperate.
sentences.zh: 毒蛇发起了攻击。

sentences.en: The snake had struck.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来他认为自己在耶鲁法学院感受到的那种污名，在他看来已经延续到了就业市场上。

sentences.en: So it sounds like he thinks he's seeing that stigma he felt at Yale Law School carrying over in his mind to the job market.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
